summary: A working couple talk about the daycare bill as a steady strain and wish the years away until school is cheaper.
realLife: A couple with young children say the weekly daycare bill is a strain, that the staff are paid very little, and that both paychecks are needed just to get by. They talk in plain arithmetic: they wish these years away, and they would love another child but cannot see how to manage. They speak of paid sick leave and cheaper care as what would help.
sources: https://www.opb.org/article/2026/06/16/working-parents-struggle-to-navigate-work-and-family-survey-confirms/ (public radio story on working parents and childcare)
gates: the speaker has a child under school age in paid care
both adults in the household work
the child care cost is a share of household pay
weights: whether the employer gives paid sick leave
whether the child is school age soon
inGame: reads the household's child care payment against its pay and the child care income limit in force; needs: a household cost record for care

turns.what: The speaker says the new preschool cut the bill and sleeps better.
turns.pulledBy: universal preschool or a child care income limit change reaches the household
turns.writesBack: the household's care cost falls; the stand on the program warms

turns.what: She says it is her boss, not the government, who should give sick days.
turns.pulledBy: the employer gives no paid leave
turns.writesBack: the stand names the employer as the reason

turns.what: She says her mother watches the baby so the arithmetic works.
turns.writesBack: the care cost record is lowered; the tie to the grandparent is credited
